title: VS Code extension: 'Stage hunks like this' on a hunk in the source-control diff, and a Clusters panel
description: The review happens in VS Code's source-control diff view, where the + on a hunk or file stages it. Add a small extension (in ai-workspace, installed by ixd setup) that adds 'Stage hunks like this' to a hunk's context menu, calling ixd wt stage-like <file>:<line> from TOOL-22, and a 'Clusters' tree view in the source-control sidebar listing the worktree's clusters (and TOOL-23's recipes once they exist) with a stage button per cluster and a click that opens the representative hunk. It refreshes the SCM view after staging. It only shells out to ixd; all clustering logic stays in ixd so the CLI and the review page agree.
definition-of-done:
1. Right-clicking a hunk in a worktree's diff offers 'Stage hunks like this', which stages every hunk of its cluster and refreshes the view.
2. The Clusters view lists the worktree's clusters with counts and a stage button each.
3. ixd setup installs it on a new machine (Linux and Windows).
testing-plan: 1. Open the ENG-34 worktree in VS Code, stage one cluster from the panel and one through the hunk menu; screenshot the SCM view before and after under tmp/.
unknowns: Whether the extension is published privately (vsix installed by ixd setup) or loaded from the ai-workspace folder as a development extension.
